Subject: Follow-up from today — usage profile & procurement questions

Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — super helpful. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can get procurement involved:

- Primary use: document summarization + contextual search for engineering docs (internal + customer support).
- Expected traffic (initial pilot): ~8M tokens/month. If pilot succeeds, expand to ~35–50M tokens/month within 3–6 months.
- Latency target: median < 500ms for chat/generation flows.

Procurement questions:
1) What pricing bands do you recommend for the 8M -> 50M monthly range? Any committed volume pricing or tiered discounts?
2) We have standard procurement thresholds: contracts > $50k need VP legal review; anything > $200k requires exec procurement sign-off. Can you flag where Redwood pricing for the initial 12 months would fall?

Appreciate a one-page cost estimate we can share with procurement + an outline of next steps.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of ML Platforms
Novalytics

Subject: RE: Follow-up from today — usage profile & procurement questions

Alex — thanks for the clear recap. Recapping here so procurement has what they need and so we can align on unit economics. Attaching a one-pager that breaks down cost per 1M tokens across hosted and committed options. (attachment: redwood-pricing-1M-token-breakdown.pdf)

Short answers up front:
- For 8M tokens/month (pilot) — hosted, pay-as-you-go run rates: ~ $1,200–$1,600/month (approx $150–$200 / 1M tokens) depending on model mix and average generation length.
- For 35–50M tokens/month — committed (reserved) pricing brings unit to ~ $40–$100 / 1M tokens depending on commitment term and model quantization choices. Typical targets we see are $50–$80 / 1M tokens with a 12–24 month commit.
- Breakpoint for procurement thresholds: if annualized committed spend > $50k, you’ll move into VP legal review; > $200k triggers exec procurement flow. For 35M tokens/month at $60 / 1M tokens, annual spend ~ $25k/month -> $300k/year (this would cross your exec procurement threshold).

Quick ask: can you confirm whether Novalytics would be comfortable with a 12-month committed minimum for production rollout? That will determine the discount band we can offer and whether we can route to our dedicated capacity discounts and single-tenant pricing.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm preferred pilot model mix + average generated tokens per request (helps refine unit cost).
2) If willing to consider 12-month commit, we will prepare a committed pricing term sheet and draft SOW (we have a template to start).
3) Introduce procurement (copying them here works) and we’ll share the one-pager + redlines template.

Looping in Dylan (cc) who will outline dedicated/reserved capacity pricing and procurement-friendly contract options.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Alex — quick procurement note from the pricing/solutions side.

If Novalytics is likely to hit 35–50M tokens/month within 3–6 months, we strongly recommend a 12-month reserved capacity with quarterly true-ups. Example pricing illustrative (subject to final model mix):
- Pilot (8M/mo) PAYG: $160 / 1M tokens -> ~$1,280/mo.
- Reserved 12-mo (35M/mo): $60 / 1M tokens effective -> ~$2,100/mo -> ~$25,200/yr.
- Reserved 12-mo (50M/mo): $48 / 1M tokens effective -> ~$2,400/mo -> ~$28,800/yr.

Notes:
- The above assumes standard open-model selection (quantized weights) — if you need single-tenant or custom model hosting, add-on applies.
- For procurement: we can stage discounts (pilot credits -> committed discount) so the first 1–2 months of pilot cost can be credited toward the commitment if you convert. That keeps pilot friction low but gives you predictable economics.

If the annualized committed spend will cross your $200k threshold we can prepare exec packet (SLA, SOC2 artifacts, customer references) in parallel to speed sign-off. Rishi — can you prepare a short note on SOC2 + data residency for the packet?

Dylan
Director, Solutions & Pricing | Redwood Inference
